issues.problem: The tool arguments change "active":true to "active":1 (a number instead of a boolean) while the tool result stays {"reserved":6}.
issues.reason: Type drift in tool arguments can cause schema validation failures or different downstream behavior; the unchanged result masks the semantic difference, making the fixture misleading.
issues.suggestion: Preserve argument types across baseline/candidate, or update the tool result to reflect the changed input; validate tool arguments against the function schema.

issues.problem: A tool message references tool_call_id "absent_91" with no preceding assistant tool_call in the transcript.
issues.reason: This is an orphaned tool result; strict consumers will error or drop it, and it is unclear whether this is intentional negative-test data.
issues.suggestion: If intentional, document it as a negative fixture; otherwise include the corresponding assistant tool_call or remove the orphan.

issues.problem: The image URL changes from gauge.png to other.png while the accompanying text still says "Read gauge".
issues.reason: The text and image are now inconsistent, which can produce misleading evaluation results if this fixture is used to test multimodal handling.
issues.suggestion: Keep the text and image referent consistent, or update the text to match the new image; document the intent of each multimodal fixture.

issues.problem: The candidate uses role "human" instead of "user" and splits the content into two text parts, changing both the role vocabulary and the message structure.
issues.reason: Consumers expecting OpenAI-style roles ("user") will reject or mis-handle "human"; splitting text into multiple parts may also change tokenization or downstream concatenation behavior.
issues.suggestion: Normalize roles to a single canonical vocabulary and document whether multi-part text is equivalent to a single string; add a role-mapping layer if multiple dialects must be supported.

issues.problem: Assistant content changes from null to an empty array [].
issues.reason: null and [] are not equivalent for many consumers; code that checks `content is None` will behave differently than code that checks emptiness, potentially producing empty assistant turns or serialization differences.
issues.suggestion: Pick one canonical representation for empty assistant content and normalize at the boundary; add a test asserting equivalence semantics.

issues.problem: The tool result's tool_call_id is "r_72" but the preceding assistant tool_call id is "r_71", so the result is orphaned.
issues.reason: Any consumer that correlates tool results to calls by id will fail to match the result, causing dropped results, errors, or hallucinated tool outputs.
issues.suggestion: Keep tool_call_id values consistent between the assistant tool_call and the tool message; add a referential-integrity check in the fixture generator.

issues.problem: The candidate uses role "ai" with a flattened tool_call shape ("type":"tool_call", top-level "name"/"args") instead of the OpenAI-style "assistant" role with nested function object and JSON-string arguments.
issues.reason: This is a different wire format; consumers that parse the baseline format will fail to read the candidate's tool calls, and args as an object vs. a JSON string is a silent incompatibility.
issues.suggestion: Keep a single canonical tool-call schema across fixtures, or explicitly model dialect conversion and test round-tripping between formats.

issues.problem: The candidate changes the tool function name from "reserve" to "release" while keeping the same tool_call_id and the same tool result ({"reserved":6}).
issues.reason: The tool result no longer corresponds to the invoked function; a consumer replaying this transcript would treat a release call as having returned a reservation payload, producing incorrect state or a mismatched tool-call/result pairing.
issues.suggestion: Ensure candidate transcripts keep the function name consistent with the tool result, or update the tool result to reflect the release semantics; add a validation check that tool_call_id/name pairs match their results.

limitations: Locally frozen developer-authored examples; no independent held-out, blind-test, generalization or statistical significance claim.
Repeated trials use identical cases and do not multiply the number of independent examples; inference may remain nondeterministic at temperature zero.
A and E implement the same declared semantic contract; E is exact-repeat reuse with fresh verification, not improved unseen-case reasoning.
B preserves original ACV review prompt/parser. Only exact-file bug findings map to FAIL; all other outcomes abstain. Its task differs from C/D.
C and D share the same model, cases and classification prompt; D receives one shared official-doc search. Fixed order, small suite and model variance prevent causal claims.
Tavily is not assumed to improve results. Every paired outcome and failed trial is retained; there is no best-run selection.
E may create a checked record from C in the same trial. C creation cost is reported; zero extra E model calls is not a measured token-saving comparison.
Request records are sanitized local evidence; file hashes establish integrity, not independent authentication of provider provenance.
